_about: Expert knowledge layer for Iconography Detective. Each saint has a title pattern (to find works in the NGA collection), optional exclusions, a short hagiographic note, and a list of attributes. Each attribute has regex patterns (case-insensitive, Python/JS compatible) that are searched for in the NGA visual description, the NGA keyword terms, and the title. Sources for the attributes: James Hall, Dictionary of Subjects and Symbols in Art; George Ferguson, Signs & Symbols in Christian Art; Jacobus de Voragine, The Golden Legend.

universal.label: Halo
universal.why: A ring or disk of light marking holiness. Common in medieval gold-ground painting; it thins to a faint ring and often disappears as painters pursued naturalism in the 15th–17th centuries.

saints.name: Saint Jerome
saints.title: \bJerome\b
saints.blurb: Scholar and Doctor of the Church who translated the Bible into Latin (the Vulgate). Artists show him two ways: the learned scholar in his study, or the penitent hermit in the Syrian desert beating his breast with a stone.

attributes.label: Lion
attributes.why: In The Golden Legend Jerome removes a thorn from a lion's paw; the grateful lion stays with him. (The story was likely borrowed from Saint Gerasimus, whose name sounds like Geronimus.)

attributes.label: Cardinal's hat / red robes
attributes.why: An anachronism: cardinals did not exist in Jerome's day, but his service as secretary to Pope Damasus led later artists to dress him as one.

attributes.label: Book / writing
attributes.why: His translation of the Bible; the scholar-in-his-study type.

attributes.label: Study / interior
attributes.why: The scholar type: Jerome at work in a book-lined study, made famous by Antonello da Messina and Albrecht Dürer.

attributes.label: Skull
attributes.why: A memento mori, meditation on death. Increasingly common from the late 15th century on.

attributes.label: Stone (penitence)
attributes.why: The penitent Jerome strikes his chest with a stone, recalling his account of temptation in the desert.

attributes.label: Crucifix
attributes.why: Object of his prayer in the wilderness.

attributes.label: Wilderness / cave
attributes.why: His years as a hermit in the desert of Chalcis.

attributes.label: Bare chest / ascetic body
attributes.why: Ascetic self-denial; the emaciated or muscular nude penitent became a showcase for anatomy.

attributes.label: Hourglass
attributes.why: Passing time, a vanitas symbol.

attributes.label: Trumpet of Judgment
attributes.why: Jerome wrote that he always heard the trumpet of the Last Judgment.

saints.name: Saint Catherine of Alexandria
saints.title: \bCatherine\b|\bCaterina\b
saints.blurb: A learned princess who out-argued pagan philosophers and refused to marry the emperor. A spiked wheel meant to torture her shattered at her touch; she was then beheaded.

attributes.label: Spiked wheel
attributes.why: The breaking wheel that miraculously shattered (origin of the 'Catherine wheel').

attributes.label: Sword
attributes.why: The instrument of her beheading.

attributes.label: Crown
attributes.why: Her royal birth.

attributes.label: Book
attributes.why: Her learning and her debate with the fifty philosophers.

attributes.label: Martyr's palm
attributes.why: General symbol of martyrdom (victory over death).

attributes.label: Ring / mystic marriage
attributes.why: In a vision the Christ Child placed a ring on her finger — the 'Mystic Marriage of Saint Catherine'.

attributes.label: Rich dress / jewels
attributes.why: Royal status, contrasted with the humble dress of most saints.

saints.name: Saint Sebastian
saints.title: \bSebastian\b
saints.blurb: A Roman soldier revealed as a Christian, tied up and shot with arrows. He survived, was nursed by Saint Irene, and was later clubbed to death. Invoked against plague, since arrows were an old image of plague striking suddenly.

attributes.label: Arrows
attributes.why: His first martyrdom.

attributes.label: Bound to tree / column
attributes.why: He was tied to a stake, tree or column as a target.

attributes.label: Nearly nude body
attributes.why: Renaissance artists made Sebastian a vehicle for the idealized male nude.

attributes.label: Archers
attributes.why: Narrative scenes show the soldiers shooting.

attributes.label: Irene tending him
attributes.why: The widow Irene nursed him back to health — a popular 17th-century subject.

attributes.label: Soldier's armor
attributes.why: His identity as an officer of the Praetorian Guard.

saints.name: Saint Peter
saints.title: \bPeter\b
saints.blurb: Fisherman, leader of the apostles, first bishop of Rome. Christ gave him 'the keys of the kingdom of heaven.' He was crucified upside down at his own request, feeling unworthy to die as Christ did.

attributes.label: Keys
attributes.why: Matthew 16:19 — the keys of heaven; often one gold and one silver.

attributes.label: Upside-down cross
attributes.why: His martyrdom in Rome.

attributes.label: Book
attributes.why: The Epistles of Peter.

attributes.label: Rooster
attributes.why: He denied Christ three times before the cock crowed; scenes of his tears of repentance.

attributes.label: Boat / fish / net
attributes.why: His trade as a fisherman on the Sea of Galilee.

attributes.label: Tears / repentance
attributes.why: The 'Penitent Saint Peter', a favourite Counter-Reformation theme of repentance.

attributes.label: Short gray curly beard
attributes.why: Conventional portrait type: older man, short curly gray hair and beard.

saints.name: Saint Paul
saints.title: \bPaul\b
saints.exclude: Vincent de Paul|Peter Paul|Paul Revere|Paolo|Paul the Hermit
saints.blurb: Pharisee who persecuted Christians until he was struck blind on the road to Damascus; then the great missionary and letter-writer of the early Church. As a Roman citizen he was beheaded rather than crucified.

attributes.label: Sword
attributes.why: Instrument of his beheading (and the 'sword of the Spirit', Ephesians 6:17).

attributes.label: Book / letters
attributes.why: His Epistles.

attributes.label: Bald head, long dark beard
attributes.why: An early portrait convention, already fixed in Early Christian art.

attributes.label: Fall from horse
attributes.why: The Conversion on the Road to Damascus (Acts 9).

attributes.label: Blinding light
attributes.why: The light from heaven that struck him blind.

saints.name: Saint John the Baptist
saints.title: John the Baptist|\bBaptist\b|Giovannino|Infant Saint John|Young Saint John
saints.blurb: The prophet who lived in the wilderness, preached repentance, and baptized Christ in the Jordan. Beheaded at the request of Salome. Often appears as a child playing with the infant Christ.

attributes.label: Lamb
attributes.why: He called Christ 'the Lamb of God' (John 1:29).

attributes.label: Reed cross / staff
attributes.why: A thin cross of reed, pointing to Christ's coming sacrifice.

attributes.label: Camel-hair garment
attributes.why: Matthew 3:4 — 'raiment of camel's hair.'

attributes.label: Scroll 'Ecce Agnus Dei'
attributes.why: The inscription 'Behold the Lamb of God.'

attributes.label: River / baptism
attributes.why: The Baptism of Christ in the Jordan.

attributes.label: Head on a platter
attributes.why: His martyrdom, presented to Salome.

attributes.label: Pointing gesture
attributes.why: The forerunner who points toward Christ.

saints.name: Saint Mary Magdalene
saints.title: Magdal
saints.blurb: Follower of Christ, witness of the Crucifixion and first witness of the Resurrection. Western tradition merged her with the sinful woman who anointed Christ's feet, making her the model of the penitent.

attributes.label: Ointment jar
attributes.why: She anointed Christ's feet, and came to anoint his body at the tomb.

attributes.label: Long loose hair
attributes.why: She dried Christ's feet with her hair; in the desert her hair grew to cover her body.

attributes.label: Skull
attributes.why: Penitence and meditation on death, in her later hermit life.

attributes.label: Crucifix
attributes.why: Her presence at the Crucifixion; devotion.

attributes.label: Mirror / jewels (vanity)
attributes.why: Her worldly life before conversion — sometimes shown being cast off.

attributes.label: Tears / upturned eyes
attributes.why: The ecstatic penitent, a key Baroque type.

attributes.label: Book
attributes.why: Contemplative life and reading of scripture.

saints.name: Saint George
saints.title: \bGeorge\b
saints.blurb: A soldier-saint whose legend (popularized by The Golden Legend) has him kill a dragon that terrorized a city and rescue a princess. Patron of knights, England, Genoa and many others.

attributes.label: Dragon
attributes.why: The dragon of Silene, symbol of evil and paganism.

attributes.label: Horse
attributes.why: He is a mounted knight.

attributes.label: Armor
attributes.why: His identity as a soldier (in 15th-century art, dressed as a contemporary knight).

attributes.label: Lance / sword
attributes.why: He wounds the dragon with his lance (often shown broken), then finishes it with a sword.

attributes.label: Princess
attributes.why: The king's daughter offered to the dragon.

attributes.label: Red-cross banner / shield
attributes.why: The cross of Saint George.

saints.name: Saint Francis of Assisi
saints.title: \bFrancis\b|\bFrancesco\b
saints.blurb: Son of a wealthy merchant who renounced everything to live in poverty and founded the Franciscan order. In 1224 on Mount La Verna he received the stigmata — the wounds of Christ — from a seraph.

attributes.label: Stigmata
attributes.why: The wounds of the Crucifixion, received in a vision of a crucified seraph.

attributes.label: Brown/gray habit with knotted cord
attributes.why: Franciscan habit; the three knots stand for poverty, chastity and obedience.

attributes.label: Tonsure
attributes.why: Shaved crown of a friar.

attributes.label: Skull
attributes.why: Meditation on death, especially in Counter-Reformation images.

attributes.label: Crucifix
attributes.why: Devotion to Christ's Passion.

attributes.label: Birds / animals
attributes.why: The Sermon to the Birds; the wolf of Gubbio.

saints.name: Saint Anthony Abbot
saints.title: \bAnthony\b|\bAntony\b|\bAntonio\b
saints.blurb: Egyptian hermit, father of Christian monasticism, famously tormented by demons in the desert. The Antonine order, which cared for victims of ergotism ('Saint Anthony's fire'), kept pigs that roamed freely wearing bells.

attributes.label: Demons / temptation
attributes.why: The Temptation of Saint Anthony — a showcase for fantastic imagery (Schongauer, Bosch, Callot).

attributes.label: T-shaped staff
attributes.why: The tau cross / crutch of the aged hermit and of the Antonine hospitals.

attributes.label: Pig
attributes.why: The Antonines' privileged pigs; later read as the demon of gluttony subdued.

attributes.label: Bell
attributes.why: Bells worn by Antonine pigs, or rung to drive away demons.

attributes.label: Fire
attributes.why: 'Saint Anthony's fire' (ergotism), which he was invoked against.

attributes.label: Long white beard / hermit
attributes.why: He lived to about 105, and is always shown as an old monk.

saints.name: Saint Christopher
saints.title: \bChristopher\b|\bCristoforo\b
saints.blurb: A giant who wished to serve the greatest king and ferried travelers across a river. One night a child he carried grew impossibly heavy: it was Christ, bearing the weight of the world. 'Christopher' means Christ-bearer.

attributes.label: Christ Child on shoulder
attributes.why: The literal 'Christ-bearer.'

attributes.label: River
attributes.why: The ford where he carried travelers.

attributes.label: Staff / uprooted tree
attributes.why: His staff, which flowered the next day as a sign.

attributes.label: Orb / globe
attributes.why: The child carries the world — the reason for the weight.

attributes.label: Hermit with lantern
attributes.why: The hermit who told him to serve Christ by helping travelers lights the way.

saints.name: Saint Michael the Archangel
saints.title: \bMichael\b
saints.blurb: Leader of the heavenly army who cast Satan out of heaven (Revelation 12), and the angel who weighs souls at the Last Judgment.

attributes.label: Wings
attributes.why: He is an angel.

attributes.label: Devil / dragon underfoot
attributes.why: The defeat of Satan, war in heaven.

attributes.label: Sword / spear
attributes.why: Commander of the angelic host.

attributes.label: Scales
attributes.why: Weighing of souls (psychostasis) at the Last Judgment.

attributes.label: Armor
attributes.why: The warrior angel.

saints.name: Saint Barbara
saints.title: \bBarbara\b
saints.blurb: Shut in a tower by her pagan father, she had a third window added to honor the Trinity. Her father beheaded her and was then struck by lightning — so she became patron of artillerymen, miners, and anyone facing sudden death.

attributes.label: Tower (with three windows)
attributes.why: Her imprisonment; three windows for the Trinity.

attributes.label: Chalice and host
attributes.why: She was invoked so as not to die without the last sacraments.

attributes.label: Martyr's palm
attributes.why: Martyrdom.

attributes.label: Crown
attributes.why: Virgin martyr's crown.

attributes.label: Book
attributes.why: Learning and faith.

attributes.label: Sword
attributes.why: Her beheading.

saints.name: Saint Lawrence
saints.title: \bLawrence\b|\bLaurence\b|\bLorenzo\b
saints.blurb: Deacon of Rome, roasted alive on a gridiron. Legend says he joked, 'Turn me over, this side is done.' When ordered to hand over the Church's treasures, he presented the city's poor.

attributes.label: Gridiron
attributes.why: Instrument of his martyrdom.

attributes.label: Deacon's dalmatic
attributes.why: His office as deacon.

attributes.label: Martyr's palm
attributes.why: Martyrdom.

attributes.label: Fire
attributes.why: The burning coals beneath the gridiron.

attributes.label: Book
attributes.why: Deacons read the Gospel at Mass.

saints.name: Saint Bartholomew
saints.title: \bBartholomew\b|\bBartolomeo\b
saints.blurb: One of the Twelve Apostles, said to have preached in Armenia, where he was flayed alive. Michelangelo painted his own face on the flayed skin Bartholomew holds in the Sistine Last Judgment.

attributes.label: Flaying knife
attributes.why: Instrument of his martyrdom.

attributes.label: Flayed skin
attributes.why: He is sometimes shown holding his own skin.

attributes.label: Book
attributes.why: Apostles carry the Gospel.

attributes.label: Dark beard
attributes.why: Conventional apostle type.

saints.name: Saint Andrew
saints.title: \bAndrew\b|\bAndrea\b
saints.blurb: Fisherman and brother of Peter, the first called of the apostles. Tradition says he was crucified on an X-shaped cross at Patras — the saltire on the flag of Scotland.

attributes.label: X-shaped cross
attributes.why: His martyrdom; he felt unworthy of a cross like Christ's.

attributes.label: Cross (any)
attributes.why: Even when not clearly X-shaped, a large cross is his sign.

attributes.label: Fish / net
attributes.why: His trade as a fisherman.

attributes.label: Long white/gray beard
attributes.why: Conventional portrait type: elderly, with long divided beard.

attributes.label: Book
attributes.why: Apostle and preacher.

saints.name: Saint Roch
saints.title: \bRoch\b|\bRocco\b|\bRoche\b
saints.blurb: French pilgrim who nursed plague victims in Italy, caught the plague himself, and withdrew to a forest where a dog brought him bread. Hugely popular in plague-era Europe, alongside Sebastian.

attributes.label: Plague sore on thigh
attributes.why: He lifts his tunic to show the bubo of plague.

attributes.label: Dog with bread
attributes.why: The dog that fed him in the forest.

attributes.label: Pilgrim's hat, staff, shell
attributes.why: He was a pilgrim to Rome.

attributes.label: Angel
attributes.why: An angel tended his wound.

saints.name: Saint James the Greater
saints.title: \bJames\b|\bJacopo\b|\bGiacomo\b|\bSantiago\b
saints.blurb: Apostle, brother of John, first apostle to be martyred. His relics at Santiago de Compostela made him the patron of pilgrims; the scallop shell became the badge of the pilgrimage.

attributes.label: Scallop shell
attributes.why: Badge of pilgrims to Compostela.

attributes.label: Pilgrim's staff
attributes.why: The pilgrim's staff and water gourd.

attributes.label: Pilgrim's hat
attributes.why: Broad-brimmed traveling hat.

attributes.label: Book
attributes.why: Apostle.

attributes.label: Sword
attributes.why: He was beheaded by Herod Agrippa.

attributes.label: Horse (Matamoros)
attributes.why: Spanish legend of his miraculous appearance at the battle of Clavijo.

saints.name: Saint John the Evangelist
saints.title: John the Evangelist|John Evangelist|Patmos|John the Divine
saints.blurb: The 'beloved disciple', traditionally author of the fourth Gospel and of Revelation, written in exile on the island of Patmos. Usually shown young and beardless — unlike the other apostles.

attributes.label: Eagle
attributes.why: His Gospel soars like an eagle (the four living creatures of Ezekiel and Revelation).

attributes.label: Chalice with serpent
attributes.why: He blessed a poisoned cup, and the poison left it as a snake.

attributes.label: Book / writing
attributes.why: Author of the Gospel and Revelation.

attributes.label: Youthful, beardless
attributes.why: The youngest apostle.

attributes.label: Vision in the sky
attributes.why: The visions of Revelation, e.g. the Woman Clothed with the Sun.

saints.name: Saint Gregory the Great
saints.title: \bGregory\b|\bGregorio\b
saints.blurb: Pope and Doctor of the Church. His secretary Peter the Deacon reported seeing the Holy Spirit as a dove at Gregory's ear as he dictated his writings. (This was one of the examples from our guest lecture.)

attributes.label: Dove at his ear
attributes.why: The Holy Spirit inspiring his writing.

attributes.label: Papal tiara
attributes.why: His office as pope.

attributes.label: Book / writing
attributes.why: His sermons, letters and the Dialogues.

attributes.label: Mass of Saint Gregory
attributes.why: Christ as Man of Sorrows appeared on the altar while Gregory said Mass — a popular late-medieval indulgence image.

attributes.label: Papal cross-staff
attributes.why: Staff of the papal office.
